title: Scalability I: block-diagonal weights
blurb: Parameter growth with relations, block-diagonal regularisation and its catch

hook.title: Too many translators
hook.text: Every relation hires its own full translator for every layer. With 100 relations, that's 100 huge books of vocabulary per layer, which is expensive and prone to **overfitting** (a translator learns quirks of a rarely-used road). One cheap fix: make each translator a **team of specialists** that each handle only a *slice* of the vocabulary. Half the books (or a quarter), but the specialists never talk to one another.
hook.recall: Remember the specialist teams: block-diagonal matrices cut parameters by the number of blocks $B$, but features in one block can’t interact with features in another.

explore.intro: Compare parameter counts. First the *Block-diagonal* tab.
tasks: Set $d^{(l+1)}=d^{(l)}=64$, $|R|=100$, $B=4$. How many parameters do you save?
Look at the 6×4 matrix with 2 blocks: which inputs affect which outputs?
explore.takeaway: Full: $d^{(l+1)}\times d^{(l)}$ per relation per layer. With $B$ blocks: $B\times\frac{d^{(l+1)}}{B}\times\frac{d^{(l)}}{B}=\frac{d^{(l+1)}d^{(l)}}{B}$. Catch: no mixing between blocks.

build.prompt: $W_r$ is $6\times4$ and we use 2 diagonal blocks. **Predict the number of parameters** (the full matrix has 24).
build.reveal: Each block is $\frac62\times\frac42=3\times2=6$ parameters; two blocks give 12: half of 24 (slide 25).

questions.prompt: Why is the number of RGCN parameters a problem?
options: It grows rapidly with the number of relations, leading to overfitting
questions.explanation: Each relation has $L$ matrices of size $d^{(l+1)}\times d^{(l)}$.

questions.prompt: $d^{(l+1)}=64$, $d^{(l)}=64$, one relation, $B=4$ blocks. Parameters of the block-diagonal $W_r$?
What is the drawback of block-diagonal weight matrices?
options: Features in one block can only be transformed by the corresponding sub-matrix and don’t interact with features in other blocks
questions.explanation: The specialist teams never talk to one another.

options: With $B$ blocks the parameters drop from $d^{(l+1)}d^{(l)}$ to $B\cdot\frac{d^{(l+1)}}{B}\cdot\frac{d^{(l)}}{B}$
Block-diagonal and basis learning are two ways to regularise the weights
In a block-diagonal matrix with 2 blocks, $x_1$ can influence the second block’s outputs
In a 6-dim vector with 2 blocks, $x_1,x_2,x_3$ are transformed only by $W_1$
questions.explanation: There’s no way for $x_1$ to influence $x_4$ (slide 28).

questions.prompt: *“Block-diagonal matrices keep all the expressive power of the full matrix while using $1/B$ of the parameters.”* What’s wrong?
options: They lose cross-block feature interaction: dims 1–3 only affect dims 1–3
